messages: maya: heads up — a couple devs reported missing images on the new migration preview, looks like relative image paths inside example notebooks are resolving to /assets/old/... instead of the new /static/... paths joel: ack, can you paste one of the broken URLs? maya: sure — in the rendered page: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/python/examples/llm-runner -> image shows broken link to /assets/old/notebooks/llm-diagram.png (404) sam: that path format rings a bell — did we change mkdocs 'docs_dir' or the theme/static handler in the last deploy? anya: I updated the mkdocs config in the migration PR (refs PR #4123) to use theme_dir overrides, but I tried to keep assets mirrored. maybe I missed a plugin mapping maya: the notebooks are built by a prepublish script that copies `examples/notebooks/*` into site/assets/notebooks/ earlier in the pipeline. The new theme expects `static/` instead of `assets/` so the copy step needs to adjust docs-bot: CI build failed on main at step: copy-examples; see logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/8372 (exit code 1) :warning: joel: ok, so two things — (A) fix the copy step to place images under `static/notebooks/` and (B) make sure any hardcoded references in markdown/notebooks use relative paths like `./notebooks/llm-diagram.png` so the site generator rewrites them consistently sam: quick question: some notebooks embed absolute paths inside HTML output cells (nbconvert). Those are harder to rewrite — should we postprocess the notebook outputs to replace `/assets/old/` with `/static/`? anya: yeah I ran into that — nbconvert produces inside the html cell. I can add a tiny sed pass that updates the src attributes during the build maya: +1 for sed pass, but also we should avoid committing absolute paths in source notebooks. I'll open a small cleanup PR to change the markdown references to relative ones joel: for safety, add a 2nd step in docs pipeline that runs linkcheck on the generated site and fails CI if any 4xx are detected for internal links. We already have linkcheck, but it's shallow — make sure it follows local static assets too sam: noted. I'll update the pipeline: run `mkdocs build` -> run `scripts/normalize-assets.sh` -> run `pytest -k linkcheck` -> deploy. The normalize script will: 1) copy notebooks -> static/notebooks, 2) sed-replace old paths inside built html anya: small gotcha: our redirect rules (Netlify _redirects) still map /examples/* -> /sdk/python/examples/* and that was masking some missing images during manual tests. We should audit redirects before making final changes maya: good catch. I'll add a redirect test to the linkcheck suite to ensure that redirected URLs still resolve 200 after rewrite docs-bot: reminder: docs CI quota is low tonight; heavy rebuilds might queue. :hourglass_flowing_sand: joel: for the PRs: @anya can you do the normalize script and test in a draft PR? @maya will do the notebook path cleanup PR. Sam will update the pipeline + linkcheck rule. I'll review both PRs and coordinate a small docs deploy window tomorrow morning 06:00 UTC to minimize impact anya: working on it, will push a draft by EOD with the sed pass and unit test for nbconvert output replacement maya: started the notebook cleanup branch: replacing absolute asset refs with `./notebooks/...` and removing lingering `site:` frontmatter that was causing some pages to be put under /old/ paths sam: about that frontmatter — we had a few pages with `slug: /old/path` which explains additional anchor/redirect confusion. Let's add a lint rule to flag `slug` that begins with `/old/` or `assets/` joel: yes — add it to the docs linter (scripts/lint-frontmatter.py). If lint fails, CI should block merging. maya: one more thing — I noticed code blocks in several notebook READMEs use triple backticks without language tags which caused the syntax highlighter to produce weird long lines that overflow the mobile layout. I'll add language tags where appropriate (```python) and run a formatter on those files anya: tiny follow-up: for the sed pass I'll make it idempotent (run it twice -> same result) and add a fallback mapping file in `docs/config/asset-mappings.json` just in case we need to remap other old prefixes sam: thanks. Also adding a short note in the migration guide (docs/migration/static-assets.md) so future contributors know about the `static/` vs `assets/` difference joel: plan sounds good. If everything passes in staging, we do the deploy tomorrow 06:00 UTC and monitor the site for 30 mins. If any 404 spikes, rollback immediately maya: will monitor analytics and CloudFront logs during the window. tagging @ops for the rollout anya: draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-ai/docs/pull/4178 (normalize script + tests) maya: cleanup PR: https://github.com/redwood-ai/docs/pull/4179 (notebook path fixes + codeblock lang tags) sam: pipeline PR: https://github.com/redwood-ai/docs/pull/4180 (linkcheck + lint + deploy gating) joel: I'll queue reviews and request quick approvals from eng-sre if tests look good maya: thanks all :pray: anya: thanks! :rocket: docs-bot: CI status update — build 8379 queued, ETA ~12m."
